<SUMMARY>Global geopolitical tensions intensified this week, marked by stalled US-Iran peace talks and Hezbollah's rejection of a ceasefire, leading to concerns over energy markets and regional stability. Concurrently, the AI and semiconductor sectors saw significant investment and strategic policy shifts, with Japan funding domestic chip production and the European Union advancing plans for tech sovereignty. Trade frictions persisted between the United States and China, centering on export controls and critical component supply chains. The smart manufacturing market is projected for substantial growth, alongside continued developments in critical mineral resources across Africa and the Americas.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>Stalled US-Iran peace talks and Hezbollah's rejection of a ceasefire indicate a heightened risk of conflict escalation in West Asia, with the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continuing to strain global energy flows. The IAEA's declaration of a drone attack on the UAE Barakah nuclear plant, attributed to pro-Iran militants, represents a serious compromise of nuclear safety and raises concerns for critical infrastructure. Persistent US export controls targeting China's semiconductor and PCB industrial supply chains, met with Chinese accusations of disruption, suggest an intensifying economic and technological decoupling with potential broad supply chain vulnerabilities for AI and defense sectors. Broadcom's AI chip guidance has prompted supply-chain questions across the Asia-Pacific region, highlighting potential bottlenecks.</EWS>
<EXEC>

**Asia:**
The Smart Manufacturing Market is projected to reach USD 995.67 billion by 2032 from an estimated USD 380.21 billion in 2026, growing at a CAGR of 17.4%. DayOne Data Centers announced the final closing of its Series C Equity Financing at US$4.5 billion and secured over 1GW renewable energy in Malaysia through a partnership with TNB. Rapidus Corporation completed a 150 billion yen (approximately $943 million USD) funding round from the Information-Technology Promotion Agency (IPA), Japan. Indonesia plans to implement plain packaging for cigarettes and vapes as part of health ministry regulations. Indonesia also secured 3 million euros in funding from Switzerland to support its bid for OECD membership. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) is positioned at the center of the AI compute supply chain. China stated that US abuse of export controls disrupts global semiconductor industrial and supply chains, and Huawei executives credit bans for accelerating domestic chip independence. Artificial intelligence companies from Taipei warn of bottlenecks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing signed a major AI deal with Nvidia.

**Europe:**
The EU trade chief called for a new diversification instrument to compel companies to seek different suppliers in critical sectors away from China. Europe is shaping its digital future through "Chips Act 2.0" proposals, putting demand at the center of its semiconductor strategy and confirming photonics as a structural addition to EU policy. Europe unveiled a sweeping tech sovereignty package to boost chips, cloud, and AI domestically, expressing concerns over reliance on US technology and a potential "kill switch."

**Americas:**
Morgan Stanley Wealth Management and Galaxy Digital announced a referral arrangement for eligible clients to lend cryptocurrency and receive shares of exchange-traded products with exposure to crypto. Anthropic, after filing for its IPO, suggested that AI model makers need to slow down their development. Keel Infrastructure priced an upsized $400 million convertible note offering at 1.250% due 2032 to fund data center buildout. USD.AI provided $98.1 million in three-year debt financing to support the deployment of 2,304 NVIDIA B300 GPUs managed by Hydra Host. The TerraSpark Energy Campus in West Virginia received an $18.5 million U.S. Department of Energy grant for a power and carbon capture project. The US stock market saw the Nasdaq and S&P 500 set for a low opening, while the price-weighted Dow was on track to rise for the third straight week, with Nvidia, Intel, Micron, AMD, and Broadcom shares under scrutiny. Asia tech stocks dropped after Broadcom's AI trade guidance, which also affected Wall Street names. Dutch chipmaker Nexperia, facing the loss of its China operations, plans to produce in the United States. OpenAI's CFO stated that AI fluency is becoming a dealbreaker for finance hires. Chinese-made circuit boards beneath AI chips are raising national security concerns in the U.S.

</EXEC>
<LITHO></LITHO>
<REE>

**Africa:**
Viridian Metals highlighted copper-rich zones up to 4.15% Cu at Kraken ahead of its 2026 drill program in Labrador. CMOC, operating the biggest copper mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo, offered bonuses and threats to end a strike that briefly crimped output this week. Brazil sits on one of the largest lithium reserves, with little exploration so far, while the world focuses on extracting lithium from Congo and Chile.

**Europe:**
Greenland Mines Ltd. moved quickly on the Sarfartoq Rare Earth Magnet Project, with a site team inspecting drill rigs on an Arctic plateau days after signing to acquire the project. Greenland is an autonomous territory of Denmark.

**Americas:**
Viridian Metals highlighted copper-rich zones up to 4.15% Cu at Kraken ahead of its 2026 drill program in Labrador. Brazil holds vast lithium reserves that remain largely unexplored, contrasting with global efforts in Congo and Chile.

</REE>
<GEO>

**Asia:**
China stated that the U.S. abuse of export controls disrupts global semiconductor industrial and supply chains, and China hit back at the US's semiconductor export controls, citing an OECD report. The US is targeting China's PCB grip, citing mounting AI and defense supply risks.

**Americas:**
The United States is assessing its options for trade war policies, and Ford CEO Jim Farley made an admission about the Xiaomi SU7, indicating that America is watching advanced and affordable technology drive by while China and other regions have access to it. US national security concerns have been raised regarding Chinese-made circuit boards hidden beneath AI chips.

</GEO>
<MILITARY>

**Europe:**
The Europe Defense Semiconductor Market is projected to reach USD 7.18 billion by 2035, driven by defense technology investments.

**Americas:**
MACOM announced new additions to its RF and optical portfolio designed for the SATCOM industry. The U.S. Defense Semiconductor Market is expected to reach USD 11.92 billion by 2035. The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) is assessing U.S. military options toward Cuba in the context of a potential Caribbean crisis and has established a commission on U.S. Cyber Force Generation.

</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>

**Europe:**
Nvidia's RTX Spark has enhanced Arm's position as a significant threat in the PC market.

</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>AirTrunk committed $30 billion to build 5GW of AI data centers in India. India's semiconductor ambitions are intertwined with energy reforms, as highlighted in the Energonomics Podcast. IMARC Engineering expanded its EPCM, ESG Compliance, and Plant Setup Advisory Services to support manufacturing growth across key sectors in India. Hindustan Zinc plans to double its metal capacity and revenue, aiming to increase metal reserves from 13 million tonnes to 50 million tonnes and support a mine life of over 25 years.</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>Wall Street futures traded lower as Hezbollah rejected a new ceasefire in Lebanon, and investors awaited U.S. jobs data. Stocks slid as US-Iran peace talks stalled and the AI rally cooled, with oil prices remaining little changed. The U.S. added 172,000 jobs in May, showing market resilience despite the ongoing Iran war, which has contributed to painfully high energy prices. US President Donald Trump stated the United States will win the conflict with Iran either "militarily or on paper," and suggested he could meet with Iran's Supreme Leader "if it was to make a deal." The head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) declared a recent drone attack on the Barakah nuclear plant in the UAE a serious compromise of nuclear safety, with the United Arab Emirates blaming pro-Iran militants for the incident. The war in Iran has entered its third month, with US-Iran negotiations remaining under pressure amid a fragile ceasefire that has been violated several times. The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues to strain global energy flows. The US and Iran are weighing an extension of their ceasefire by two weeks. India's energy security is at a crossroads due to the Hormuz crisis, presenting an opportunity for US-India cooperation. The US energy secretary stated that lower gas prices would ultimately require a resolution with Iran. A Russian executive suggested the US is using the Strait of Hormuz to "reshape" energy markets. The economic fallout of the Iran war is a subject of ongoing discussion.</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The current geopolitical landscape is characterized by persistent high tensions in West Asia, primarily driven by the ongoing Iran war and its impact on global energy security, alongside complex US-Iran negotiations. The global technology sector is witnessing a race for AI and semiconductor dominance, marked by significant investments in data centers and foundry capabilities in Asia, while Europe pushes for tech sovereignty. Intensifying trade and export control measures between the US and China are reshaping global supply chains, raising critical vulnerabilities in defense and AI component production. These dynamics suggest a fragmented global economic and technological order, necessitating strategic diversification and heightened vigilance for supply chain resilience and regional stability.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
